instructions.title: Prepare Mushrooms and Pork
instructions.text: Rehydrate dried wood ear and shiitake mushrooms in hot water for 20-30 minutes. Drain, squeeze out excess water, remove shiitake stems, and thinly slice both types of mushrooms. Julienne the pork loin into thin strips.

instructions.title: Combine Broth and Aromatics
instructions.text: In a large pot or Dutch oven, bring the chicken broth to a simmer over medium-high heat. Add the sliced pork, rehydrated mushrooms, and julienned bamboo shoots. Cook for 5 minutes, ensuring the pork is cooked through.

instructions.title: Season the Soup Base
instructions.text: Stir in the rice vinegar, soy sauce, and white pepper. Taste and adjust seasonings as needed; you may want more vinegar or pepper depending on your preference for 'hot' and 'sour'.

instructions.title: Add Tofu and Thicken
instructions.text: Gently add the julienned firm tofu to the simmering soup. Stir the cornstarch slurry thoroughly, then slowly pour it into the soup while continuously stirring. Continue to stir until the soup thickens to your desired consistency.

instructions.title: Add Egg Ribbons
instructions.text: Reduce heat to low. Slowly drizzle the beaten egg into the simmering soup in a thin stream, stirring gently in one direction to create delicate egg ribbons. Do not overmix.

instructions.title: Finish and Serve
instructions.text: Remove the soup from heat. Stir in the sesame oil. Ladle the Hot and Sour Soup into individual bowls. Garnish generously with chopped green onions and a drizzle of chili oil, if desired, before serving hot.

tips: For authentic flavor, do not skimp on the white pepper and rice vinegar; they are key to the 'hot' and 'sour' balance. Adjust them to your personal taste.

If you cannot find wood ear mushrooms, fresh shiitake mushrooms can be used, but dried ones offer a more intense, earthy flavor. You can substitute pork with chicken or omit for a vegetarian version with vegetable broth.
Hot and Sour Soup is best served immediately. If reheating, gently warm on the stovetop and add a fresh drizzle of sesame oil and green onions to revive the flavors.
article:
Craving a bowl of soup that’s as exciting as it is comforting? Look no further than Hot and Sour Soup, a quintessential Chinese classic that tantalizes the taste buds with its complex symphony of flavors. This isn't just any soup; it's a culinary journey, balancing fiery heat with tangy sourness, savory umami, and a satisfying array of textures. Often found on menus from bustling dim sum parlors to elegant fine dining establishments, Hot and Sour Soup has captivated palates worldwide. But why just order it when you can master this delightful dish in your own kitchen? Get ready to explore the depths of this beloved creation and, by the end of this article, you'll be well-equipped to prepare your very own, incredibly authentic Hot and Sour Soup recipe.

## What is Hot and Sour Soup?

Hot and Sour Soup, or Suan La Tang (酸辣汤) in Mandarin, is a staple of Chinese cuisine, particularly popular in the Sichuan and Hunan provinces, known for their bold and spicy flavors. At its heart, it's a savory broth, typically chicken or pork-based, that achieves its signature "hot" from white pepper and, sometimes, chili oil, and its "sour" from rice vinegar. Beyond these primary flavor profiles, the soup boasts a rich umami depth from ingredients like soy sauce and dried mushrooms.

The texture is as important as the taste. Hot and Sour Soup is usually thickened to a silky consistency with a cornstarch slurry, giving it a luxurious mouthfeel. Suspended within this delightful broth are an assortment of finely shredded or diced ingredients: tender strips of pork, delicate tofu, crunchy bamboo shoots, earthy dried shiitake mushrooms, and chewy wood ear mushrooms. A final flourish of whisked egg ribbons adds a visual appeal and another layer of texture. It's a dish that engages all senses, offering warmth, spice, and a refreshing tang, making it an ideal appetizer or a light meal on its own. Understanding these components is key to a successful Hot and Sour Soup recipe.

## Ingredients You Need

Crafting an authentic Hot and Sour Soup recipe requires a blend of common pantry items and a few specialty Chinese ingredients easily found in Asian markets or even well-stocked supermarkets. Gathering the right ingredients is the first step toward a perfect Hot and Sour Soup recipe.

*   **For the Broth Base:**
    *   6 cups Chicken or Vegetable Broth (high quality makes a difference!)
*   **Proteins:**
    *   4 oz Pork Loin or Tenderloin, thinly shredded (or substitute with chicken breast, shrimp, or omit for vegetarian)
    *   4 oz Firm Tofu, pressed and cut into small strips or cubes
*   **Mushrooms & Vegetables:**
    *   1/4 cup Dried Shiitake Mushrooms, rehydrated, stems removed, thinly sliced
    *   1/4 cup Dried Wood Ear Mushrooms, rehydrated, thinly sliced (or fresh if available)
    *   1/2 cup Bamboo Shoots, thinly shredded
    *   2 tbsp Lily Flowers (dried, optional, rehydrated)
*   **Flavor & Seasoning:**
    *   1/4 cup Rice Vinegar (black vinegar can be used for a deeper, earthier sourness)
    *   3 tbsp Soy Sauce
    *   1 tsp Dark Soy Sauce (for color, optional)
    *   1-2 tsp White Pepper (start with 1 tsp, adjust to taste for the "hot")
    *   1 tsp Sesame Oil
    *   1-2 tsp Chili Oil (optional, for extra heat)
    *   Pinch of Sugar (to balance flavors)
*   **Thickener & Binder:**
    *   3 tbsp Cornstarch mixed with 4 tbsp cold water (cornstarch slurry)
    *   1 Large Egg, lightly beaten
*   **Garnish:**
    *   2 Green Onions, thinly sliced
    *   Fresh Cilantro (optional)

## Step-by-Step Instructions

Follow these steps to create an authentic and flavorful Hot and Sour Soup recipe in your own kitchen. Precision and timing are key to achieving that perfect balance.

1.  **Prepare Dried Ingredients:** If using dried shiitake and wood ear mushrooms, place them in separate bowls and cover with hot water. Let them rehydrate for at least 30 minutes, or until soft. Once soft, drain, squeeze out excess water, remove shiitake stems, and thinly slice both types of mushrooms. If using lily flowers, rehydrate them as well.
2.  **Prep Remaining Ingredients:** Thinly shred the pork loin. Press the tofu to remove excess water and cut it into small strips or cubes. Slice bamboo shoots. Have all your seasonings (vinegar, soy sauce, white pepper) measured and ready. Prepare your cornstarch slurry by whisking cornstarch with cold water until smooth. Lightly beat the egg in a small bowl.
3.  **Bring Broth to a Boil:** Pour the chicken or vegetable broth into a large pot or Dutch oven and bring it to a rolling boil over medium-high heat.
4.  **Add Meats & Vegetables:** Once boiling, add the shredded pork to the broth. Cook for 1-2 minutes until it's no longer pink. Then, add the rehydrated shiitake mushrooms, wood ear mushrooms, bamboo shoots, and tofu. Bring the soup back to a simmer.
5.  **Season the Soup:** Stir in the rice vinegar, soy sauce, dark soy sauce (if using), white pepper, and a pinch of sugar. Taste and adjust. This is where you fine-tune the "hot" and "sour" balance. Add more white pepper for heat, more vinegar for sourness, or a touch more soy sauce for saltiness/umami.
6.  **Thicken the Soup:** Give the cornstarch slurry a quick whisk again (as starch settles) and slowly pour it into the simmering soup in a thin stream, stirring constantly. Continue stirring until the soup thickens to your desired consistency. It should be viscous enough to coat a spoon lightly, but not gloopy.
7.  **Add Egg Ribbons:** While the soup is still simmering, slowly pour the beaten egg into the soup in a thin stream, stirring gently in a circular motion. This will create delicate, beautiful egg ribbons. Cook for about 30 seconds until the egg is set.
8.  **Finish and Serve:** Remove the soup from heat. Stir in the sesame oil and chili oil (if using). Ladle the Hot and Sour Soup into bowls. Garnish generously with sliced green onions and fresh cilantro, if desired. Serve immediately.

## Pro Tips for the Best Results

Even with a great Hot and Sour Soup recipe, a few insider tips can elevate your dish from good to unforgettable.

*   **Quality Broth is Key:** A flavorful broth forms the foundation of this soup. Use a high-quality store-bought broth, or even better, homemade chicken stock for the deepest flavor.
*   **Balance is Everything:** The "hot" and "sour" are personal preferences. Start with the recommended amounts of white pepper and vinegar, then taste and adjust gradually. Don't be afraid to add a little more of either until it perfectly suits your palate. A pinch of sugar can help balance the sourness and enhance other flavors.
*   **Don't Rush the Thickening:** When adding the cornstarch slurry, pour it in slowly while stirring constantly. Wait a minute after adding to see if it reaches your desired thickness before adding more. You can always add more slurry, but you can't easily thin it out once it's too thick.
*   **Egg Technique:** For delicate egg ribbons, ensure the soup is simmering (not boiling vigorously) and pour the beaten egg in a very thin, slow stream while gently stirring the soup in a single direction. Don't overcook the egg; it sets quickly.
*   **Freshness Matters:** While dried mushrooms are essential for their unique flavor, ensure they are fully rehydrated. Fresh ingredients for garnish also make a big difference in presentation and taste.
*   **Let it Mingle:** While best served fresh, the flavors of Hot and Sour Soup can sometimes deepen and meld even more beautifully after sitting for a short while.

## Serving Suggestions

Hot and Sour Soup is incredibly versatile and can be enjoyed in various ways.

*   **Appetizer Extraordinaire:** It's a classic starter for any Chinese meal, whetting the appetite without being too heavy.
*   **Light Meal:** Paired with a bowl of steamed white rice, it transforms into a satisfying and comforting light lunch or dinner.
*   **Part of a Feast:** Serve it alongside other popular Chinese dishes like General Tso's chicken, Kung Pao shrimp, or vegetable lo mein for a complete culinary experience.
*   **Garnish Galore:** Don't forget the garnishes! Freshly chopped green onions are a must, adding a fresh, pungent bite. A sprinkle of fresh cilantro, a drizzle of extra chili oil for more heat, or even a few drops of roasted sesame oil can elevate the presentation and flavor.

## Variations and Substitutions

While this classic Hot and Sour Soup recipe is fantastic as is, it's also incredibly adaptable to different tastes and dietary needs.

*   **Vegetarian/Vegan Hot and Sour Soup:** Easily made vegetarian by omitting the pork and using vegetable broth. For a vegan version, also omit the egg (or use a plant-based egg substitute) and ensure your soy sauce is vegan-friendly. Extra tofu or rehydrated soy curls can add more protein.
*   **Different Proteins:** Instead of pork, try thinly shredded chicken breast, small shrimp (add them in the last few minutes of cooking so they don't overcook), or even thinly sliced beef.
*   **Spice Level:** Adjust the "hot" to your liking. Increase or decrease the amount of white pepper. For a more intense, layered heat, add a dash of chili oil or a few drops of Sichuan peppercorn oil.
*   **Sourness Profile:** While rice vinegar is standard, some recipes use Chinese black vinegar for a deeper, maltier sourness. You can use a blend of both.
*   **Mushroom Medley:** Experiment with different types of mushrooms. Fresh shiitake, oyster mushrooms, or even button mushrooms can be used in addition to or in place of dried varieties for varied textures and flavors.
*   **Extra Vegetables:** Feel free to add other thinly sliced vegetables like carrots, snow peas, or even spinach in the last few minutes of cooking for added nutrition and color.
*   **Gluten-Free:** Ensure your soy sauce is gluten-free (tamari works well) and verify that your broth does not contain gluten. Cornstarch is naturally gluten-free.

Whether you stick to the traditional Hot and Sour Soup recipe or experiment with variations, the joy of creating this iconic Chinese soup at home is immense. Its intoxicating aroma, vibrant flavors, and comforting warmth make it a dish you'll want to revisit again and again. So, gather your ingredients, follow these steps, and prepare to impress yourself and your loved ones with a bowl of truly spectacular Hot and Sour Soup. Enjoy the journey!
